interactions.summary: Jiang explains that each universe metaphor changes perception differently, then sketches what several options imply: energy as chaos, soul as fractal mirroring, cave as simulation, God as the mind or dream containing us, garden as divine cultivation, and factory as lawful machinery.
A student clarifies that the 'ball' metaphor means something like a crystal ball holding everything inside it, while Jiang tries to locate what kind of order that image implies.

Jiang asks what a body signifies as a universe metaphor, and students answer that it means we are part of the universe, can reflect on it, contain everything within an organized whole, act through organs with distinct purposes, and may even map onto the body of Christ.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led discussion with multiple student answers

claims.claim: Jiang explicitly says that the metaphor chosen for the universe changes how the universe is perceived.
Jiang says an energy metaphor makes the universe appear as chaos and randomness.
Jiang says a soul metaphor makes the universe fractal, with the human soul mirroring the entire cosmos.
Jiang treats the cave metaphor as a simulation and the God metaphor as living inside the mind or dream of God.
Jiang says the garden metaphor implies God as gardener who nurtures and cultivates us, while the factory metaphor implies a machine governed by laws.
In the body metaphor, students and Jiang converge on the idea that we are really part of the universe, that its parts are interconnected, and that organs have distinct roles working together.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang makes metaphor into ontology: whichever image you choose for the universe changes what sort of world you think you live in.
signature_moments.source_phrase: depending on the metaphor you will perceive the universe in a different way
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's governing insight and explains why the brainstorm matters rather than functioning as classroom decoration.

signature_moments.moment: The soul image turns the cosmos into a fractal where the individual soul mirrors the whole universe.
signature_moments.source_phrase: your soul is a universe and then it mirrors the entire universe
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is Jiang's sharpest positive alternative to chaos and prepares the later move toward a body structured by meaning.

signature_moments.moment: The body metaphor becomes compelling because it means we are not outside the universe looking in; we are part of it and capable of reflecting within it.
signature_moments.source_phrase: we are like really part of the universe and that we can also reflect
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves the interactive, self-implicating character of the body image before Jiang turns it into a full theory of purpose and intentionality.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's use of the soul metaphor to describe the universe as a mirrored pattern in which the soul contains the structure of the whole.
The universe understood as an organized living whole whose parts belong together, serve distinct purposes, and may act through a coordinating center.

chronology_notes.note: This packet performs the interpretive turn promised by the brainstorm: Jiang now sorts the candidate metaphors and begins to privilege the body image by extracting connection, role, and reflexivity from it.

uncertainty_notes.note: The student's 'ball' clarification is semantically slippery, and Jiang himself sounds unsure how to classify it, so it should be kept as exploratory rather than stabilized into a strong lecture concept.
